title: Google’s November Pixel update is missing, and Android 17 QPR2 may explain why
summary: November's missing update has sparked an intriguing theory.
body: TL;DR November Pixel update hasn’t arrived, breaking the first-Tuesday release pattern that Google has followed for most monthly updates this year. Android security database entries and reported release candidate builds suggest Android 17 QPR2 could arrive earlier than its expected December release. Google hasn’t confirmed an early QPR2 rollout or explained the November update’s absence. Google’s Pixel update calendar has been quite predictable this year, until November apparently went off-script. Regular security patches have generally landed on the first Tuesday of the month, while bigger Android releases have taken a little longer. But November’s first Tuesday has come and gone without an update, raising an interesting question: Is Google preparing something bigger than the usual security fixes? A Reddit user believes the answer could be Android 17 QPR2, which has generally been expected in December.

title: Anthropic rolls out Claude Personal Finance with spending analysis and bill tracking
summary: Claude wants to understand your money, not spend it.
body: TL;DR Anthropic is rolling out Claude Personal Finance in beta to Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers in the US. Users can connect bank and credit card accounts to analyze spending, track upcoming bills, and spot unusual charges. Connections use Plaid with read-only access, meaning Claude cannot move or invest money, and users don’t have to share their banking passwords with the assistant. Banks are putting up warning signs at the vault while AI companies are building new doors into it. Bank of America recently cautioned customers against sharing their banking passwords with AI assistants, even as it champions AI’s potential in banking. Meanwhile, OpenAI has already introduced financial account connections in ChatGPT , while Google’s Gemini can analyze spending through its Wallet integration . Now Anthropic is joining the money conversation, betting that Claude can help you understand your finances without touching your cash. The company has officially unveiled Personal Finance in Claude , a feature we first spotted taking shape in September . It’s rolling out in beta this week to Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers in the US.

Snapdragon processors are usually the preferred platform for more demanding emulators, and that’s largely due to the proliferation of custom Turnip GPU drivers. We’ve seen a few attempts to deliver similar GPU drivers and utilities on non-Snapdragon devices, but the ARMSX2 emulator made a big splash with MaliSX2 last month. title: New Android exploit only needs you to install an app to wreck your phone
summary: Android sabotages itself next.
body: TL;DR Bitdefender researchers discovered an Android vulnerability that can trigger an endless crash loop simply by installing a specially crafted APK, potentially leaving devices unusable. The flaw exploits how Android handles ZIP compression methods, repeatedly crashing the core system_server process. Recovering may require a factory reset or manually deleting the malicious file using ADB. No in-the-wild exploitation has been identified, but the public disclosure could make it easier for threat actors to develop an exploit. Even though Android is a relatively safe operating system, with several security measures in place , threat actors’ ingenuity still keeps finding ways to exploit weaknesses. We recently shared information about malware that can empty your bank accounts in secret , and now, researchers have found a separate Android flaw that could leave your phone outright unusable. Normally, malicious apps need to request permissions and execute code to attack your device. However, researchers at Bitdefender have discovered a new vulnerability dubbed GhostMap that triggers a crash loop simply by installing a specially crafted app.
